marble.description: Construct and interpret a box plot on a numerical scale from a five-number summary (minimum, lower quartile, median, upper quartile, maximum), using the stated convention that the whiskers extend to the minimum and maximum values; interpret the median, quartiles, IQR and range, recognising that each whisker and each ha
marble.prompt: If you sees box plots comparing how long two classes spent on homework, could they say which class had the higher middle time and which was more spread out — and explain why a longer whisker doesn't mean more children are in that part?

cluster.summary: Your child is learning to organise and count information by sorting objects into groups and comparing which groups have more or fewer items.

misconceptions: 'The longer whisker must contain more of the people.'
representations: Aligned dot plot and box plot
authoredAnswer: IQR 9, range 22. Correct scaled construction labels all five values. The longer upper whisker shows more value spread, not more observations; raw counts, mean and individual gaps are not supplied.

wrongAnswers.revealedBy: Treats plotted numerical length as frequency. Source basis: AAMT Top Drawer Teachers, Features of box plots, five-number summary and linked display discussion. The child-voice wording is an authored diagnostic adaptation
wrongAnswers.fix: Align the box plot with original ranked observations and count cases within each quarter.

before.name: Quartiles and interquartile range
before.reason: A box plot is drawn from the five-number summary, which requires finding the median and quartiles

before.name: Histograms
before.reason: Comparing a box plot with a histogram of the same data helps show which features of the distribution a box plot cannot reveal

before.name: Describing distributions
before.reason: Explaining what a box plot hides (clusters, gaps, shape) requires being able to describe those features of a distribution

after.name: How far apart two groups are
